newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan late-trade stocks higher despite SFC move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan late-trade stocks higher despite SFC move.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were higher in late Wednesday trade, largely unrattled by the Securities and Futures Commission's launch of what it called a routine probe into credit trading practices in the stock market.
The commission denied the move aimed to cool down the red hot stock market.
With 60 minutes left, at 0300 GMT, the index was up 40.80 points or 0.46 percent at 8,958.97.
Turnover was a brisk T$95 billion.

"Investors interpreted the SFC move as aiming not to cool down the market, but to eliminate speculation, which is good for the market in the long run," said Taiwan International Securities assistant vice-president Alex Chiu.
Electronics, which was once hit by the SFC news and fell 0.99 percent, were up 0.97 percent, with chipmaker Mosel up the daily seven percent limit to T$70.5.
"Investors continue to favor electronics most despite the sector's recent surge," Chiu said.
Paper, steel and financial shares were also strong.
A firming trend was seen, brokers said.
